CASE-001.question: What is a contract account?

context_items.title: Contract Accounts
context_items.text: This component enables you to create and manage contract account master data. In Contract Accounts Receivable and Payable, each business partner posting is assigned to one business partner and to one contract account. In the contract account master record, you can define, for each business partner, the procedures that apply when posting and processing the line items of a given contract account. These include, for example, payment and dunning.

context_items.text:

CASE-004.question: What is an installation in SAP Utilities?

context_items.title: Move-in
context_items.text:
You use the move-in function to carry out most of the activities required to begin providing a business partner with a utility service. You create new, or change existing business master data. Most importantly, you allocate a contract to an installation.
In move-in processing, you establish whether a contract can be billed. From the move-in, you can also trigger the charges levied at the commencement of a utility service, as well as a welcome letter to the customer.
context_items.rendered_text:

context_items.title: Move-in
context_items.text:
To create a move-in, you require one or more installations that are vacant on the desired move-in date.
- In the case of an initial move-in, ensure that you have completed initial data creation, including creation of the installation(s).
- Devices can (but do not have to) be installed and allocated before move-in.
- If one of the installations is already allocated to a contract, this allocation must be reversed. To do this, process a move-out. An installation can only be allocated to one contract at any given time.

context_items.title: Move-in
context_items.text:
Customer Contact
When a move-in is created, a corresponding customer contact is created automatically. This is automatically linked to the move-in document. You can find additional information in the section on Customer contact .
Overall Check
When a contract is assigned the move-in status 05 (meter reading entered completely), you can verify that the contract can be billed.
Move-In Status
If you process or display a move-in document, the system also displays the move-in status of each contract. The move-in status informs the agent which stage of move-in processing has been reached.
The minimum is formed from the move-in status of the contracts and also displayed. In this way you can obtain information on the status of the entire move-in processing.
Move-In Documents
When you display the move-in documents for a business partner or a premise, the documents from the last three months appear. If no documents exist for this period then the system displays the documents from the last six months.

CASE-006.question: What is a budget billing plan?

context_items.title: Budget Billing Plan
context_items.text:
Utility companies normally bill for their services at the end of a supply period - in an annual consumption billing, for example. Therefore, they charge budget billing amounts during the supply period instead of the actual amount owed, in order to remain solvent. You specify the budget billing amounts and the dates that are due in the budget billing plan. The budget billing plan is the basis for charging budget billing amounts.
With budget billing plans, you manage the budget billing requests in a billing period in between two periodic bills.
You can use several budget billing procedures. Each of these have different ways of determining budget billing dates and amounts, managing budget billing data, and posting procedures:
- Statistical budget billing procedure
- Partial bill procedure
- Payment plan procedure
- Payment scheme

CASE-008.question: What is clearing control in incoming payments?

context_items.title: Clearing Control in Incoming Payments
context_items.text:
During the processing of externally initiated payments, the system attempts in event 0110 to assign the payment amount to the open items. By default, the system posts unassigned amounts and partial amounts of a payment on account.
Clearing control takes account of entries in the same fields, as in account maintenance . Additional postings, such as payments on account and expense and revenue postings, can also be set up.

CASE-009.question: What is an installment plan in FI-CA?

context_items.title: Installment Plan
context_items.text: With an installment plan you divide source items to several installment receivables that have a due date in the future. Once an installment plan has been posted, the items of the installment plan and not the source items are referred to when a bank collection is made, or when a dunning run is carried out.

Once an installment plan has been posted, the items of the installment plan and not the source items are referred to when a bank collection is made, or when a dunning run is carried out.

context_items.title: Installment Plan
context_items.text: You create an installment plan for business partners wishing to make payment but who are temporarily unable to keep up their payment obligations. One or more source items can form part of an installment plan. However, only receivables and items in the same currency and in one contract account can be included in an installment plan.

context_items.title: Installment Plan
context_items.text: An installment plan consists of a statistical document with several installment receivables. The individual installment receivable is cleared upon payment. The number of the installment plan is saved in the source items. This ensures a connection between the installment plan and the source receivables, and between the source receivables and the installment plan. If interest is payable on an installment plan, the installment plan will also have an interest supplement.

CASE-016.question: What estimation procedures are available in meter reading?

context_items.title: Estimation Procedure
context_items.text:
If measurement data is incomplete or implausible, it may be necessary to replace or add to this data with estimated values. Data simulations and forecasts are also based on estimations. In SAP Utilities, estimation procedures are used in the following processes:
- Estimate meter reading results
- Validate meter reading results
- Billing simulation
- Budget billing plan creation
- Unbilled revenue reporting
The estimation procedures used are extrapolation and interpolation . When using the quantity determination procedure Quantity Determination During Meter Reading , both of these procedures use the quantities saved in the system for the respective base period as a basis for estimation. The system uses these quantities to calculate the quantity for the estimation period and then calculates the estimated value for the meter reading.

In this case, the gas factors are determined for the most recent actual previous meter reading result. This part of the concept is described in section Interaction - Estimation and Meter Reading .

context_items.text: In the system receivables are submitted in two steps. First you have to release the items for collection. Then you can submit the released items. context_items.title: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
context_items.text:
This component enables you to manage disconnections and reconnections. This component is optional. You need to use it if you want to temporarily interrupt supply to customers (especially within the bounds of a legal dunning procedure). A disconnection is a temporary interruption in the supply of a utility service that does not involve the meter removal. This is due to the following reasons, for example:
- Introduction of a collection procedure for outstanding payment
- Technical disconnection due to request of utilities company or customer
In the first instance, the service is resumed (reconnection) when the customer has paid the outstanding bill; in the second, it is done at the request of the customer.

CASE-025.question: How do I create a budget billing plan?

context_items.title: Budget Billing Plan
context_items.text:
Utility companies normally bill for their services at the end of a supply period - in an annual consumption billing, for example. Therefore, they charge budget billing amounts during the supply period instead of the actual amount owed, in order to remain solvent. You specify the budget billing amounts and the dates that are due in the budget billing plan. The budget billing plan is the basis for charging budget billing amounts.
With budget billing plans, you manage the budget billing requests in a billing period in between two periodic bills.
You can use several budget billing procedures. Each of these have different ways of determining budget billing dates and amounts, managing budget billing data, and posting procedures:
- Statistical budget billing procedure
- Partial bill procedure
- Payment plan procedure
- Payment scheme

CASE-034.question: How does a utility installation disconnection lead to reconnection?

context_items.title: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
context_items.text:
This component enables you to manage disconnections and reconnections. This component is optional. You need to use it if you want to temporarily interrupt supply to customers (especially within the bounds of a legal dunning procedure). A disconnection is a temporary interruption in the supply of a utility service that does not involve the meter removal. This is due to the following reasons, for example:
- Introduction of a collection procedure for outstanding payment
- Technical disconnection due to request of utilities company or customer
In the first instance, the service is resumed (reconnection) when the customer has paid the outstanding bill; in the second, it is done at the request of the customer.

CASE-041.question: Why do utility companies charge budget billing amounts?

context_items.title: Budget Billing Plan
context_items.text:
Utility companies normally bill for their services at the end of a supply period - in an annual consumption billing, for example. Therefore, they charge budget billing amounts during the supply period instead of the actual amount owed, in order to remain solvent. You specify the budget billing amounts and the dates that are due in the budget billing plan. The budget billing plan is the basis for charging budget billing amounts.
With budget billing plans, you manage the budget billing requests in a billing period in between two periodic bills.
You can use several budget billing procedures. Each of these have different ways of determining budget billing dates and amounts, managing budget billing data, and posting procedures:
- Statistical budget billing procedure
- Partial bill procedure
- Payment plan procedure
- Payment scheme

heading_path: Submission of Receivables to Collection Agency
context_items.text: In the system receivables are submitted in two steps. First you have to release the items for collection. Then you can submit the released items. The collection items created are recorded in the system. You can carry out the release and submission of the items manually, automatically as a mass run, or automatically in other business transactions. The system can determine the collection agency to which the receivables are to be submitted automatically during release or you can specify a collection agency when you submit. For the submission, the system checks whether the items entered manually or selected by the release run have a status that permits submission. For each collection agency, it creates a list and/or a submission file with all information relevant for collecting the receivables and calls the corresponding API for the submission. You can generally submit all items with Receivable Released for Submission (01) or Receivable Called Back (09) status.

- Partial bill procedure
- Payment plan procedure

CASE-046.question: What is disconnection of an installation?

context_items.title: Disconnection/Reconnection of a Utility Installation
context_items.text:
This component enables you to manage disconnections and reconnections. This component is optional. You need to use it if you want to temporarily interrupt supply to customers (especially within the bounds of a legal dunning procedure). A disconnection is a temporary interruption in the supply of a utility service that does not involve the meter removal. This is due to the following reasons, for example:
- Introduction of a collection procedure for outstanding payment
- Technical disconnection due to request of utilities company or customer
In the first instance, the service is resumed (reconnection) when the customer has paid the outstanding bill; in the second, it is done at the request of the customer.

context_items.text:
You use the move-in function to carry out most of the activities required to begin providing a business partner with a utility service. You create new, or change existing business master data. Most importantly, you allocate a contract to an installation.
In move-in processing, you establish whether a contract can be billed. From the move-in, you can also trigger the charges levied at the commencement of a utility service, as well as a welcome letter to the customer.

context_items.title: Move-in

- If one of the installations is already allocated to a contract, this allocation must be reversed. To do this, process a move-out. An installation can only be allocated to one contract at any given time.

context_items.title: Estimation Procedure
context_items.text:
If measurement data is incomplete or implausible, it may be necessary to replace or add to this data with estimated values. Data simulations and forecasts are also based on estimations. In SAP Utilities, estimation procedures are used in the following processes:
- Estimate meter reading results
- Validate meter reading results
- Billing simulation
- Budget billing plan creation
- Unbilled revenue reporting
The estimation procedures used are extrapolation and interpolation . When using the quantity determination procedure Quantity Determination During Meter Reading , both of these procedures use the quantities saved in the system for the respective base period as a basis for estimation. The system uses these quantities to calculate the quantity for the estimation period and then calculates the estimated value for the meter reading.

context_items.title: Estimation Procedure
context_items.text:
During extrapolation, a value is determined beyond the base period. During interpolation, a value is estimated between other existing values. The base period is the period that contains all meter readings used as the basis for estimation.
One feature of the quantity determination procedure Quantity Determination During Meter Reading for the gas division is that the quantity is calculated once an actual meter reading is available following one or more estimations (usually extrapolations). In this case, the gas factors are determined for the most recent actual previous meter reading result. This part of the concept is described in section Interaction - Estimation and Meter Reading .
With these differences in mind, you can read the information about the classical estimation procedures for discrete values:
Classical Estimation Procedure
The aspects specifically relevant for quantity determination during meter reading are described in the following sections.

This component enables you to manage disconnections and reconnections. This component is optional. You need to use it if you want to temporarily interrupt supply to customers (especially within the bounds of a legal dunning procedure). A disconnection is a temporary interruption in the supply of a utility service that does not involve the meter removal. This is due to the following reasons, for example:
- Introduction of a collection procedure for outstanding payment
- Technical disconnection due to request of utilities company or customer
In the first instance, the service is resumed (reconnection) when the customer has paid the outstanding bill; in the second, it is done at the request of the customer.

context_items.title: Automatic Billing
context_items.text:
All master data and billing master data must be consistent before billing can be executed.
This means the following:
- A business partner and a contract must be allocated to the installation in move-in processing.
- Devices containing registers must be allocated to this installation in device installation.
- Meter reading orders must be generated and meter reading results must be entered in meter reading.
- The schedule records must be created in scheduling.
- In billing, a rate determination must be defined for the rate category of the installation and for the rate type of the device/register.

context_items.text:
Automatic billing determines the amount to be paid, based on the meter reading taken for the register. Calculation rules defined in variants in the rate are used to calculate this amount. Nonmeasured consumption and demand values specified in the facts for the rate, the rate category or the installation are also taken into account.
